persona.context: Uses Web Terminal ACP to coordinate local and remote shell sessions, agent-clients, project todos, artifacts, review gates, and git worktrees for a software project.

journey.scenario: Manage one agent-driven project todo across phased work, artifacts, review, and merge
journey.trigger: A product, bugfix, research, review, or operations request needs an AI agent to work inside the project with durable context and evidence.
journey.desiredOutcome: The user can keep one requirement card as the source of truth, run research/implementation/review/fix/test phases in isolated terminals, see artifact and review evidence roll up without slowing the board or terminal, then land or follow up safely.

phases.name: Capture request
phases.userGoal: Preserve what needs to be done before starting agent work.
actions: Write a natural-language todo or ask an agent directly in a terminal
Infer scope, constraints, and validation from surrounding docs
thoughts: Is this enough context for an agent to execute without asking again?
Which parts are product decisions versus implementation details?
painPoints: Acceptance criteria, constraints, artifact needs, and stop conditions are often implicit

branches.label: Ambiguous todo
branches.condition: The agent starts implementation before the user intent and validation target are clear.

phases.name: Prepare context
phases.userGoal: Give the agent the right project knowledge without flooding the prompt.
actions: Search docs and code
Open related project todo, artifact, and previous agent record context
thoughts: The next agent should not rediscover the same architecture boundaries.
I need the context pack to include the latest project rules.
painPoints: Context is scattered across terminal history, docs, artifacts, and project todo metadata

branches.label: Context skipped
branches.condition: Small tasks bypass context preparation and later fail review because project rules were missed.

evidenceRefs: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-06-agent-development-optimization-research.md#1-agent-开发的核心资源是上下文不是模型调用次数

phases.name: Dispatch agent
phases.userGoal: Start the right agent-client in the right runtime with safe isolation.
actions: Choose a todo type, agent-client, profile, and requested artifact kinds
Launch or reuse a terminal window through the todo dispatch surface
Ensure managed shells use an agent worktree
thoughts: This task needs Codex or a specialized profile?
Will this branch be tracked and merged back cleanly?
painPoints: Manual terminal setup can overwrite the single assigned terminal or leave work outside tracked worktrees
Research, implementation, review, fix, and test work are separate user intents, but the current card mainly exposes one assigned terminal pointer

branches.label: Wrong execution lane
branches.condition: A research or review task runs with an implementation-oriented prompt or missing artifact policy.

branches.label: Phase hidden in history
branches.condition: The user opens detail history to reconstruct which terminal performed research, implementation, review, or fix work.

phases.name: Observe work
phases.userGoal: Know whether the agent is progressing without interrupting the terminal.
actions: Watch terminal output, board cards, artifact status, and agent status
Use card summaries, command history, artifacts, and worktree signals to assess state
Open todo details when multiple terminals or review runs are involved
thoughts: Is the agent blocked, testing, reviewing, or just idle?
Terminal input and output must stay instant even when status panels update.
painPoints: Status, agent record, command history, artifact polling, and worktree refreshes can compete for attention and performance budget
Board polling that opportunistically creates requested artifacts can wait behind dispatch row locks and make todo list updates feel slow
A lightweight card summary does not yet explain active phase count, participant count, artifact readiness, and blocked child work together

branches.label: Terminal latency regression
branches.condition: Non-critical status projection slows the primary terminal input/output experience.

branches.label: Board lock contention
branches.condition: Artifact scheduling from the todo list waits on dispatch updates for the same project_todos rows.

phases.name: Review evidence
phases.userGoal: Decide from artifacts and validation evidence, not the agent's self-report.
actions: Open generated terminal and project artifacts
Read changed files and work snapshot
Run or inspect validation results
Dispatch review when needed
thoughts: Did the agent run the promised checks?
Are the artifacts useful for the next decision or only decorative?
painPoints: Implementation completion, evidence presence, artifact readiness, and review approval are separate but not always visible as one gate
Project-level artifacts such as user_journey can become stale when todo and multi-agent workflows evolve

branches.label: Changes requested
branches.condition: Review finds a risk and the user sends the todo back for a fix phase.

evidenceRefs: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-06-agent-development-optimization-research.md#4-agent-质量提升依赖验证回路不是更长-prompt

phases.name: Land or follow up
phases.userGoal: Merge completed work and preserve reusable project knowledge.
actions: Merge the agent branch back to main
Update project artifacts, summaries, and follow-up todos
Preserve which terminals, artifacts, review runs, and validation evidence supported completion
Clean up worktrees when appropriate
thoughts: Is main now the source of truth?
What should future agents learn from this run?
painPoints: Completed work can remain stranded on agent branches or in terminal history if the merge and knowledge handoff are not explicit
Without a phase timeline, future users may see a done card but not the route through research, implementation, review, and fixes

branches.label: Unlanded work
branches.condition: The todo looks complete, but main does not contain the agent branch or artifact update.

phases.name: Shape task contract
phases.userGoal: Turn the request into an executable todo with just enough decision structure.
actions: Pick a todo type
Record goal, constraints, acceptance criteria, required artifact kinds, validation commands, and human checkpoints
Choose whether the work starts as a simple implementation dispatch or a phased work plan
thoughts: The agent can execute from this card without guessing the product intent.
opportunities: Use todo type defaults for agent/profile/artifact policy
Expose missing acceptance criteria before dispatch
Map product-design and user-review todos to page_review_cards plus project:user_journey maintenance
systemResponsibilities: Keep the todo contract visible to implementation, review, and artifact generation agents

phases.name: Assemble context pack
phases.userGoal: Provide a compact source-of-truth context bundle before work starts.
actions: Review generated references to AGENTS.md, relevant docs, code areas, related artifacts, prior runs, and known risks
thoughts: The context is current, scoped, and reusable across stages.
opportunities: Generate context once per todo and reuse it for implementation, review, and fix phases
systemResponsibilities: Prefer canonical project docs and current artifacts over stale terminal snippets
Mark unknowns instead of inventing facts

phases.name: Dispatch phased work
phases.userGoal: Start the selected agent-client as a tracked phase without losing the root todo context.
actions: Create a research, implementation, review, fix, test, artifact, or other ProjectTodoWorkItem when the work has phase semantics
Dispatch the work item to a new or reused terminal with the selected agent/profile/artifact contract
Create or register the linked worktree
Pass the task contract, context pack, completed phase summaries, and linked artifacts into the agent prompt
thoughts: The card remains the requirement source of truth while each phase has its own terminal and artifacts.
I can add a review or fix phase without overwriting the implementation terminal history.
opportunities: Use ProjectTodoWorkItem to avoid treating every phase as a top-level child card
Keep one main card while allowing multiple phase terminals
Promote only independently schedulable sub-requirements to child todos
systemResponsibilities: Do not allow completed work to remain only on an agent branch
Keep terminal byte stream as the display source of truth
Attach terminal, artifact, review, and work snapshot records to the correct phase and root todo

phases.name: Monitor work rollup
phases.userGoal: Understand active phases, blockers, artifacts, and risk without micromanaging each terminal.
actions: Watch board work_summary rollups for active/completed phases, participants, artifact counts, terminal count, and blocked child status
Open the latest active terminal when byte-level detail matters
Choose a specific phase terminal, artifact, or agent record from the detail timeline
Notice when artifact generation is pending because the todo is not yet artifact-ready
thoughts: I can see whether this is research, implementation, review, or fix work without opening every terminal.
The board stays responsive even while artifact requests and dispatch updates happen in the background.
opportunities: Roll up active phases, participants, artifact counts, latest terminal summary, and worktree state on the card
Show full phase detail only in the todo detail route to keep list queries light
Skip locked artifact candidates instead of making board polling wait behind dispatch row updates
systemResponsibilities: Prioritize terminal input/output over status, agent record, command history, artifact polling, and worktree refresh
Separate terminal byte-stream facts from inferred status
Keep list API projections lightweight and avoid per-card N+1 queries
Treat artifact creation from board polling as opportunistic and non-blocking

phases.name: Review gate
phases.userGoal: Approve, reject, or request fixes using structured evidence.
actions: Compare diff and artifacts against the todo contract
Check focused validation output for each relevant work item
Run review agent or human review
Create a fix phase when needed and inherit review findings into its prompt context
thoughts: The decision is grounded in artifacts, tests, and risk coverage.
opportunities: Show implementation done, evidence present, artifact-ready, and review passed as separate gate signals
Link review findings directly to fix work items
systemResponsibilities: Do not let the implementation agent be the only judge of completion
Keep review findings linked to follow-up fixes
Keep project-level artifacts current when user-facing workflow decisions change

phases.name: Land and learn
phases.userGoal: Move reviewed work into main and carry forward reusable knowledge.
actions: Merge through the serialized agent branch flow
Mark the root todo done or create follow-up cards
Preserve phase, artifact, review, validation, and merge trace on the root todo
Update project artifacts and docs when the journey changes
thoughts: Main, artifacts, and future agent context now agree.
opportunities: Treat project:user_journey as a maintained source truth for product and user-review todos
Use follow-up cards only when work is independently schedulable, not for every lifecycle phase
systemResponsibilities: Surface stale project artifacts when product behavior changes
Keep main, artifacts, and future agent context aligned after landing

branches.description: If the request lacks user goal, constraints, or validation target, pause dispatch and shape the task contract before implementation.
If a phase becomes independently schedulable or blocks other requirements, promote it to a child todo while keeping dependency semantics separate from parent-child ownership.
If the agent cannot proceed after self-service investigation, surface the blocker on the todo and preserve partial artifacts or trace evidence.
If review finds a behavioral risk, create or dispatch a fix phase that inherits the task contract, context pack, artifacts, and review findings.
If a remote client cannot run the requested artifact or agent, keep the todo pending/retryable and show the runtime reason instead of losing the artifact request.
If project artifact creation from board polling hits a todo row currently being updated by dispatch, skip that locked candidate and retry later instead of blocking the list response.
If card state, artifact polling, or worktree refresh threatens terminal responsiveness, defer secondary projections and keep the terminal byte stream authoritative.

decisionTrace.rationale: The reviewed Current journey centers Project Todo as the root user-facing work object, with phase/work-item execution, isolated terminals, artifact-backed review gates, lock-aware board polling, and explicit merge/learning closure.
decisionTrace.synthesisNarrative: This Current update keeps the prior shift away from the generic support-portal demo and folds in the June 7 project-todo research plus the same-day artifact lock-contention finding. The journey now treats one Project Todo as the source of truth while research, implementation, review, fix, test, and artifact work can run as traceable phases. It also preserves the performance constraint that terminal I/O and board/list responsiveness must not be sacrificed by artifact scheduling, status projection, or worktree refresh.

clarificationAnswers.answer: Project operator / engineering lead coordinating agent-client work in Web Terminal ACP.
clarificationAnswers.rationale: README and recent project-todo research describe Web Terminal ACP as a control plane for durable shell and AI coding agent work.

clarificationAnswers.answer: Use Project Todo as the root user-facing work object, with ProjectTodoWorkItem/phase details and linked artifacts inside the card.
clarificationAnswers.rationale: The multi-agent card research recommends keeping one main card for the requirement while aggregating research, implementation, review, fix, terminal, and artifact work.
clarificationAnswers.resultingChange: The To-Be journey now names phased work dispatch and board work_summary rollups instead of relying on a single assigned terminal pointer.

clarificationAnswers.answer: Represent lifecycle stages as work items by default, and promote only independently schedulable work to child todos.
clarificationAnswers.rationale: The research rejects creating a top-level card for every phase because that fragments the root requirement context.

clarificationAnswers.answer: Separate implementation completion, validation evidence, artifact readiness, and review approval before considering a todo done.
clarificationAnswers.rationale: The agent-development optimization research explicitly rejects relying on an agent self-report as the completion signal.

clarificationAnswers.answer: Keep todo list polling and artifact request creation opportunistic and non-blocking, including SKIP LOCKED behavior for artifact candidates.
clarificationAnswers.rationale: The slow-SQL investigation found board/list latency came from artifact scheduling waiting behind dispatch row locks rather than missing indexes.
clarificationAnswers.resultingChange: The journey adds board lock contention as an explicit branch and makes list latency plus artifact lock waits part of the To-Be monitoring metrics.

rejectedOptions.rationale: Too narrow: it covers shell persistence but misses project todo contracts, artifact requests, review gates, phase rollups, and multi-agent coordination.
Too noisy: it would split one requirement across many top-level cards even when research, implementation, review, and fix are lifecycle stages of the same todo.
This was a generic ACAS fixture and did not describe Web Terminal ACP's actual project user journey.

userEdits: Task request was to update the project's user journey, so the Current artifact is scoped to Web Terminal ACP's own project/operator journey rather than a sample support portal.
The update incorporates the latest Project Todo multi-agent/phase research and the project todo artifact lock-contention performance finding from 2026-06-07.

openRisks: The Current journey is evidence-based from project docs and recent internal research, but it has not gone through an explicit human review decision panel in this task.
ProjectTodoWorkItem, work_summary, child todo ownership, and template work plans remain product-direction concepts in the journey until their schemas, APIs, and UI surfaces are implemented.
Downstream Flow Model, Capability Map, Low-fi Prototype, UI Spec, and Glossary fixtures still contain older or unrelated demo content and should be reconciled after this User Journey update.
If artifact generation is reintroduced into board polling without candidate prefilters and SKIP LOCKED behavior, the user journey can regress to slow todo list responses during dispatch bursts.
assumptions: The project-level user journey should describe Web Terminal ACP's own operator experience rather than a generic ACAS sample.
Project Todo remains the primary user-facing work object for agent-driven development coordination.
Lifecycle phases should stay inside the root todo unless they become independently schedulable child requirements.
Terminal input/output responsiveness remains a non-negotiable journey constraint when status, artifact, and worktree projections compete for resources.
Project artifact scheduling should be opportunistic and should not block board/list reads or dispatch-stage updates.
